questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: What is a golden query set?
options: The complete log of every query production received, replayed without sampling
A maintained, versioned sample of queries that represent real information needs
The subset of queries on which the current ranking system already performs strongly
A ranked list of the documents judged most relevant across the whole collection

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: Why are production query logs a useful sampling frame?
options: They arrive with relevance labels attached, so no separate judging is required
They give every rare intent the same coverage as the frequent navigational ones
They exempt the resulting test set from privacy review and access obligations
They expose real wording, spelling errors, identifiers, and ambiguous phrasing

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: What problem does stratified query sampling address?
options: Important query classes that a uniform sample would leave with too few instances
Relevance grades that assessors apply inconsistently from one class to the next
Aggregate estimates that still need traffic weights before they can be reported at all
Duplicate wordings of one popular query that inflate its weight in the test set

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: Why maintain both a stable core and a rotating recent slice?
options: To shrink the judged set every quarter so that total assessment cost keeps falling
To guarantee that every query in the set has at least one recorded click
To keep trend lines interpretable while the set gains coverage of newer traffic
To keep assessors from ever seeing a query they have already judged before

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: Why is selecting only queries with clicks a biased construction rule?
options: It admits only queries the current analyzer already tokenizes into indexed terms
It over-represents multilingual queries, which attract clicks at a higher rate
It guarantees each clicked document was judged relevant by a human assessor
It drops abandonment and zero-result failures and mirrors the incumbent's exposure

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: A rare compliance class is 1 percent of traffic but has high failure cost. What is the best test-set treatment?
options: Oversample it as a named stratum and keep the weights needed for overall estimates
Sample it in proportion to traffic so the macro average stays unbiased by design
Assign its results the top relevance grade so regressions surface without judging
Replace it with the frequent navigational queries that exercise the same ranking path

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: How is a relevance pool normally constructed?
options: By judging every document in the collection against each evaluation query
By sampling documents uniformly at random from the whole collection for each query
By taking the top results of several systems and judging the deduplicated union
By labeling only the first result the incumbent system returns for each query

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: What is the main reason to use pooling?
options: To spend limited assessment effort where relevance is plausibly concentrated
To guarantee that no document in the collection is left unjudged for a query
To judge the incumbent system's top results before any new system's are seen
To avoid having to write an operational definition of relevance for assessors

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: What is the primary tradeoff when increasing pool depth?
options: Assessor agreement improves while the diversity of pool contributors falls
Judgment coverage improves while the assessment cost of the pool keeps growing
Graded labels collapse to binary while the per-query recall estimates get sharper
Metric stability improves while the incumbent system's advantage grows larger

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: Why should assessors be blinded to contributor and original rank?
options: Because the contributing system's name reveals the query's intended intent
Because deduplication cannot run once a contributor is attached to each row
Because the judgments would otherwise apply to only one system's result list
Because a high original rank leads assessors to expect and assign a higher grade

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: A semantic retriever is evaluated on a pool built only from lexical systems. What is the central risk?
options: Its scores fall on a different scale, so fusion weights are no longer comparable
It shares no documents at all with the lexical contributors, so its pool is empty
Its novel relevant documents go unjudged and are scored as though irrelevant
Its queries are reformulated during pooling, so the original wording is lost

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: Which evidence best supports stopping pool expansion?
options: The pool has reached the same depth used by the most recently published benchmark run
Metric ordering holds steady and added candidates yield few new relevant documents
One contributing system has now won on every single query in the evaluation set
Every contributor's top ten results have each been judged by at least one assessor

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: How should an LLM relevance judge be treated?
options: As a measurement instrument with calibration error that has to be estimated
As ground truth once its agreement with one assessor exceeds chance level
As a substitute for the written rubric, which the model infers from examples
As a ranking system whose output order supplies the labels for evaluation

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: What should a judge prompt define explicitly?
options: The scores the incumbent system assigned to each candidate being judged
The retrieval model and index version that produced each candidate document
The byte length beyond which a candidate document should be considered too long
The relevance grades and the criteria that separate one grade from the next

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: What does requiring passage evidence from an LLM judge help detect?
options: Assessors who apply the rubric more strictly than the written guideline asks
Rationales that assert support the candidate document does not actually contain
Queries whose intent note is too vague for a consistent grade to be assigned
Documents whose polished prose style inflates the grade the judge assigns

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: Why should model identifier, prompt, and truncation settings be versioned?
options: Because agreement with human assessors is guaranteed once they are all fixed
Because caching judged inputs is only permitted for prompts left unversioned
Because a change to any of them can shift labels and break reproducibility
Because grades must be made binary before a judge's output can be aggregated

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: A judge often upgrades human grade 2 to grade 3. Which metric setup can amplify the error most?
options: nDCG with exponential gain, where grade 3 is worth more than double grade 2
MAP computed after binarizing at grade 1, where both grades count as relevant
Recall at a deep cutoff, where every positive grade contributes the same amount
MRR over the same queries, where only the first positive grade is inspected

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: What is the strongest use of judge confidence in a production labeling workflow?
options: Accept every high-confidence grade without auditing any of them afterwards
Drop low-confidence queries from the evaluation set before metrics are computed
Use the confidence value itself as the relevance grade for that candidate
Route uncertain and high-impact cases to humans once confidence is calibrated

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: What do public retrieval benchmarks primarily provide?
options: Evidence that a system will meet a specific product's quality requirements
Query distributions drawn from the private traffic of the product under test
Shared corpora, metrics, and baselines that make published results comparable
An assurance that the benchmark text never appeared in model training data

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: What is a defining value of BEIR?
options: It supplies a single large homogeneous web corpus with dense relevance labels
It tests zero-shot retrieval across many datasets drawn from different domains
It measures the end-to-end latency of a retrieval system under production load
It provides in-domain training data for fine-tuning a retriever on each domain

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: Why should BEIR results be reported per dataset as well as averaged?
options: Because the datasets share one corpus, so the average double-counts documents
Because per-dataset reporting removes any risk of training-data contamination
Because the average is undefined whenever a dataset uses graded judgments
Because an average can hide gains concentrated in one domain and losses elsewhere

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: What happens when a public test split is repeatedly used to select prompts and checkpoints?
options: It becomes development data, and the reported performance is optimistically biased
It becomes more representative of production traffic with each selection round
Its relevance judgments become exhaustive, so unjudged documents disappear
Its per-dataset variance falls, so smaller differences become statistically clear

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: A model improves benchmark nDCG but makes retrieval one hundred times slower. What is the correct conclusion?
options: The gain justifies replacing the production system, since relevance is the goal
The relevance gain has to be weighed against the product's latency and cost budget
The benchmark result is invalid, because latency is part of every retrieval metric
The slowdown is irrelevant offline, since benchmark scores exclude serving cost

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: Which evaluation sequence provides the strongest evidence?
options: Tune the fusion weights on the public test split, then report that split's score
Report a single benchmark average without the configuration that produced it
Reproduce known baselines, test across domains, then validate on a private set
Skip published baselines and evaluate only on an internal set with no controls
